text:
deploy-bot: Canary rc-2026-10-02-1 finished deploy to canary-usw2. Post-deploy smoke (prefill-kvprobe) started — target 300 samples. Noting p95 +200ms and synthetic cache-miss rate up ~3.8%. tagging #eng-releases :triage_lights:

sam: seeing the heartbeat drop. is this the change that adjusted KV TTLs?

rachel: yes, rc-2026-10-02-1 includes a default kv.ttl reduction from 30s -> 5s to save mem. appears some prefills are now missing cached prefixes and regen cost is spiking.

sre-jorge: cache thrash -> extra prefix recompute -> CPU & latency spike. can we temporarily bump TTL back on canary and throttle synthetic probes while we decide?

qa-lee: repro: run the small prefill loop with env CANARY=1 and you'll see cache-miss rate jump immediately: `for i in 1..400; do curl -sS -X POST https://canary.api.redwood/v1/prefill -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'; done`

rachel: we can flip kv.ttl to 30s via config flag on the canary: `redwoodctl set-config canary-usw2 inference.kv.ttl=30s --apply` — ready to apply if ops agree.

sre-jorge: do it and also reduce synth fanout to 10rps for a 5m verification window. we don't want user lanes affected.

ops-bot: synth-fanout set=10rps for canary-usw2 by rachel. verification window 5m started.

rachel: applying TTL bump now. `redwoodctl set-config canary-usw2 inference.kv.ttl=30s --note "postdeploy emergency revert"`

ops-bot: config change applied. inference.kv.ttl=30s. Tracing: increase sample for canary-prefill to 100% for 5m.

qa-lee: immediate telemetry: cache-miss rate falling back to baseline, p95 trending down toward normal. sampled traces show fewer prefix recomputes. :white_check_mark:

sre-jorge: good. root cause confirmed: too-short KV TTL in this build causing cache thrash under probe/fanout patterns. Options: rollback build, keep TTL revert as mitig and continue canary, or patch code to make TTL adaptive.

sam: prefer keeping canary with TTL revert for now to collect telemetry on other metrics (errors, memory). schedule a follow-up fix to make TTL adaptive.

rachel: opening INF-2026-900: summary: kv.ttl reduction from 30s->5s causes cache-thrashing under synthetic fanout leading to p95 spikes. attaching traces, repro, and config diff. assigning to rachel.

ops-bot: ticket INF-2026-900 created by rachel and assigned to rachel.

sre-jorge: decision: rollout paused for user ramp, canary kept live with TTL bumped to 30s, synth throttled to 10rps for 6h, tracing at 100% for short window. implement adaptive TTL in follow-up PR before next ramp.

qa-lee: added note to release draft: "Hold: KV TTL change reverted on canary due to post-deploy cache-thrash; follow-up INF-2026-900."

sam: will monitor memory and cache metrics; if stable after 6h we can consider a controlled ramp with adaptive TTL. thanks team. :thumbsup:
